message_source_quote: White-bear steering (WBS, Raman et al. 2026) uses only think/don't-think pair items. The `directed_modulation` family has two other subfamilies (secret, preference) that also require holding a concept in mind under suppression, just with different surface wording. Pooling all three produces a direction with cosine 0.86–0.90 to WBS — closely related but distinct, with a different optimal dose (scale 5 vs 4) and better peak performance.
writeup_source_quote: Raman et al. showed a think/don't-think stance direction at layers 20–24 lifts association pass@10 from 0.14 to 0.83. The pair items are one of three ways directed_modulation elicits "holding in mind while writing": secret and preference subfamilies also hold a concept under suppression, with different wording. Pooling all three should average out content-specific noise while preserving the shared stance.
rationale: Both documents explicitly name Raman et al. 2026 / white-bear steering as the prior work the method extends, describing the same mechanism (pooling pair-pos, secret, and preference subfamilies vs. pair-neg) and the same novelty claim (a direction related but distinct from WBS's pair-only direction, cosine 0.86-0.90, with a different optimal scale 5 vs 4). The message's framing of overlap and novelty matches the write-up's Motivation/Result sections closely, with no material addition or omission regarding the source's identity, the method's relationship to it, or its claimed novelty.
